title: The run that passed too early
blurb: The draft calls a run green after a handful of samples and serves a stale report.
prompt: A release shipped on an eval run that was marked passed after 12 of 500 samples, and the report endpoint kept serving a cached copy from before the last batch. The model-generated draft gates on a caller-supplied threshold and never invalidates its cache. Review it, fix it, and prove the gate only opens on a complete, current record.
aiNote: The draft marks the run passed as soon as any sample scores above the threshold, accepts a threshold override from the query string, and serves a report cached at run start so late failures never appear.
testIdea: Start a run over 500 samples and assert it stays pending at 12 and at 199 scored samples; pass a threshold override and assert 400; finish the run below threshold and assert the report flips to failed immediately.
followUps: How many samples make a pass meaningful, and how would you bound the error?
What do you do when the judge model itself regresses mid-run?
How would you compare two runs without letting dataset drift explain the difference?
